question.stem: En el texto, la palabra «prosperan» significa:

parts.text: En muchas ciudades latinoamericanas, las azoteas y los patios traseros se han convertido en pequeños huertos. Lo que comenzó como un pasatiempo de unos cuantos vecinos es hoy una práctica extendida: familias enteras cultivan tomates, hierbas y lechugas en cajones de madera o en botellas recicladas. Quienes promueven estos huertos sostienen que sus beneficios van más allá del ahorro. Cuidar una planta exige constancia, y esa rutina, afirman, reduce el estrés y fortalece los lazos entre vecinos que intercambian semillas y consejos. Sin embargo, los especialistas advierten que un huerto urbano difícilmente abastece por completo a un hogar. El espacio es limitado, el agua cuesta y no todos los cultivos prosperan a la sombra de los edificios. Aun así, reconocen que estas iniciativas cumplen una función educativa valiosa: quienes siembran aprenden de dónde provienen sus alimentos y tienden a desperdiciar menos.

answer.rationale: En «no todos los cultivos prosperan a la sombra de los edificios», el verbo se refiere a que las plantas crecen y se desarrollan bien.

distractorRationales.A: Toma el sentido económico de «prosperar», que no se aplica a un cultivo.
distractorRationales.C: Confunde crecer con venderse; el texto no habla de comercio.
distractorRationales.D: Es el sentido contrario al del verbo.

She ______ to school by bus every day.

answer.rationale: A habitual action with a third-person singular subject takes the simple present with -es.

distractorRationales.A: Base form: it does not agree with a third-person singular subject.
distractorRationales.C: The -ing form needs an auxiliary verb.
distractorRationales.D: The past participle needs an auxiliary verb.

question.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The meeting has been postponed ______ next Monday.

answer.rationale: 'Postponed until' marks the point in time up to which something is delayed.

distractorRationales.B: 'Since' marks the start of a period that continues to the present.
distractorRationales.C: 'During' needs a period of time, not a point.
distractorRationales.D: 'At' is used with clock times, not with days.

question.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Although the instructions seemed ______ at first, most students understood them after a second reading.

answer.rationale: The contrast with 'understood them after a second reading' calls for a word meaning unclear.

distractorRationales.B: 'Generous' describes people or amounts, not instructions that are hard to understand.
distractorRationales.C: 'Reluctant' describes an unwilling person.
distractorRationales.D: 'Fragile' describes something easily broken.

question.stem: According to the passage, why did Elena Ruiz start the mobile library?

options.text: The nearest public library was far away.
The town council asked her to do it.

parts.text: Every Saturday morning, a brightly painted bus parks beside the market in San Rafael. Inside, instead of seats, there are shelves holding more than two thousand books. The mobile library was started six years ago by a retired teacher, Elena Ruiz, who noticed that the nearest public library was an hour away by road. At first, only a handful of children came. Today, more than a hundred readers of all ages borrow books each week, and volunteers offer free reading classes for adults. The town council recently offered to build a permanent library, but Ruiz has asked that the bus keep running as well. "A building waits for people," she says. "The bus goes to them."

answer.rationale: The passage states that she 'noticed that the nearest public library was an hour away by road'.

distractorRationales.B: The council appears later, offering to build a permanent library.
distractorRationales.C: The bus parks beside the market, but the market is not the reason.
distractorRationales.D: The passage does not mention schools closing.

question.stem: What does Ruiz most likely mean when she says, "A building waits for people. The bus goes to them"?

options.text: A mobile library reaches readers who would not travel to a fixed one.
A building is too expensive for a small town.
The bus is faster than walking to the market.
People in San Rafael prefer buses to libraries.

parts.text: Every Saturday morning, a brightly painted bus parks beside the market in San Rafael. Inside, instead of seats, there are shelves holding more than two thousand books. The mobile library was started six years ago by a retired teacher, Elena Ruiz, who noticed that the nearest public library was an hour away by road. At first, only a handful of children came. Today, more than a hundred readers of all ages borrow books each week, and volunteers offer free reading classes for adults. The town council recently offered to build a permanent library, but Ruiz has asked that the bus keep running as well. "A building waits for people," she says. "The bus goes to them."

answer.rationale: She contrasts a fixed library, which readers must travel to, with a bus that brings books to where they are; that is why she wants it to keep running.

distractorRationales.B: Cost is not mentioned; the council has offered to build the library.
distractorRationales.C: The quotation is about access to books, not travel speed.
distractorRationales.D: The bus is itself a library; she is not comparing preferences.

question.stem:
Which sentence correctly combines the two ideas?

The road was closed. We took a longer route.

options.text: The road was closed, so we took a longer route.
The road was closed, but we took a longer route.
Because we took a longer route, the road was closed.
The road was closed we took a longer route.

answer.rationale: 'So' expresses the result: the closed road is the reason for the longer route.

distractorRationales.B: 'But' signals a contrast, and the second idea is a consequence of the first.
distractorRationales.C: Reverses cause and effect.
distractorRationales.D: Joins two sentences with no connector or punctuation.
